title: OpenAI to Reduce Electricity Demand at New AI Centers During Peak Grid Strain
summary:
OpenAI has launched the Grid Protectors program, an initiative designed to lower the energy consumption of its upcoming AI data center campuses during periods of high demand on local power networks. The company stated it will assume all costs for electricity and the necessary grid infrastructure at these sites.

The system would be applied to OpenAI's planned campus in Georgia, which is currently in development. While the site is projected to need 3.2GW of power, the program would allow OpenAI to cut that demand by as much as 1GW during peak strain, a reduction approximately equal to the average electricity use of 700,000 homes.

selectedTweets.text:
OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors program, designed to reduce electricity use at future AI data centers when local power grids are strained.

Its planned Georgia campus is expected to require 3.2GW of power, but could reduce demand by up to 1GW during peak periods, equivalent to the average electricity use of roughly 700,000 homes.

The campus is still in development. 

OpenAI says it will cover the full electricity and grid infrastructure costs.
